glintr100-antelopev2.name: glintr100 (antelopev2) [baseline]
glintr100-antelopev2.license: InsightFace model zoo: non-commercial research use
glintr100-antelopev2.notes: The reference model for the whole benchmark. Detector in the same pack (SCRFD) is not used: inputs are already aligned.

auraface-v1.name: AuraFace-v1
auraface-v1.training_data: 'commercially and publicly available data sources' (model card)
auraface-v1.pre: ONNX, RGB, (x-127.5)/127.5, 112x112 (verified identical to InsightFace's own loader)
auraface-v1.notes: Only commercially-licensed ResNet-100 tested, but scored far below the baseline on this protocol. Cause not investigated (training data vs. alignment mismatch are both possible).

w600k-r50-buffalo-l.name: w600k_r50 (buffalo_l)
w600k-r50-buffalo-l.license: InsightFace model zoo: non-commercial research use
w600k-r50-buffalo-l.notes: Recognizer of the popular buffalo_l pack.

w600k-mbf-buffalo-s.name: w600k_mbf (buffalo_s)
w600k-mbf-buffalo-s.license: InsightFace model zoo: non-commercial research use
w600k-mbf-buffalo-s.notes: Small and fast. CoreML cannot run this model, the loader falls back to CPU automatically.

sface-opencv.name: SFace (OpenCV)
sface-opencv.pre: OpenCV cv2.FaceRecognizerSF.feature() on the aligned 112x112 BGR crop (OpenCV does its own preprocessing)
sface-opencv.notes: 128-d embedding (all others are 512-d). Commercially friendly licence, mid-to-low accuracy here.

edgeface-base.name: EdgeFace-Base
edgeface-base.arch: EdgeNeXt-based hybrid CNN/Transformer with low-rank linear layers
edgeface-base.notes: Edge-device family; 18.23M params and 1398.83 MFLOPs per the model card. Code is fetched from github.com/otroshi/edgeface at run time (not vendored).

vit-tiny8-arcface-gaunernst.notes: Tiny ViT, ~5.5M params. Output is not normalised by the model: the harness L2-normalises.

facenet-casia-webface.name: FaceNet InceptionResNetV1 (CASIA-WebFace)
facenet-casia-webface.license: code MIT (facenet-pytorch); weights terms follow training data
facenet-casia-webface.pre: PyTorch, RGB, (x-127.5)/128 at 160x160 (our 112x112 crops are bilinearly upsampled)
facenet-casia-webface.notes: Understated: FaceNet expects looser 160x160 crops than these tight 112x112 ones. Clean score (not trained on VGGFace2).

facenet-vggface2-leaked.name: FaceNet InceptionResNetV1 (VGGFace2) [LEAKED]
facenet-vggface2-leaked.training_data: VGGFace2 = the same data as this benchmark (LEAKED, not a fair score)
facenet-vggface2-leaked.license: code MIT (facenet-pytorch); weights terms follow training data
facenet-vggface2-leaked.notes: LEAKED: trained on VGGFace2, so this score is inflated and must not be compared with the others. Shown for completeness only.

clip-vit-l14.key: CLIP ViT-L/14 image encoder (LLaVA vision-tower family)
clip-vit-l14.name: CLIP ViT-L/14 image encoder
clip-vit-l14.arch: ViT-L/14 image tower (the vision-encoder family used by LLaVA)
clip-vit-l14.training_data: web image-text pairs (general purpose, not face-specific)
clip-vit-l14.notes: Included to test the 'general-purpose encoder' claim: far below face-specific models.

lvface-t.name: LVFace-T (Glint360K)
lvface-t.training_data: Glint360K (same data as the antelopev2 baseline)
lvface-t.license: model card + code: MIT. The licence file covers the code; weights / Glint360K terms NOT verified
lvface-t.notes: CoreML cannot run the ViT layers, so on Apple Silicon this runs on CPU (slow for -B). LVFace-L exists but was not run (about 3 h on this CPU; card shows it ~= -B).
